text:
Cutter Gauthier keeps doing the thing that isn't supposed to be repeatable. His three goals against Pittsburgh made it three hat tricks in five games, and Daily Faceoff noted he is the first NHL player to score three in a 10-day span to start a month. The Ducks have won five straight, and on Sunday they did it on a night when the Penguins had the better of play.

Start there, because it matters for what comes next. Pittsburgh took 73% in deserved to win (the share of replays of every shot that the Penguins win) and controlled even strength, 2.27 expected goals to 1.36. The Ducks lived on the power play, 3 for 4, and in Laurent Brossoit, who stopped 31 of 33 and saved 2.5 goals more than his shots deserved. His biggest stop came early, on a 45% look by Nick Robertson in the first period, the best chance of the night that didn't go in.

Mikael Granlund opened it on the power play on a 4% shot, the least likely goal of the game, and Gauthier added a power-play goal and an even-strength one inside three minutes of the second. By the time Tristan Luneau made it 4-0 early in the third, Pittsburgh's win chance was in single digits. Kris Letang answered with a slap shot on the power play, Rickard Rakell made it 4-2 from Sidney Crosby and Evgeni Malkin, and the Penguins chased with an extra skater until Gauthier finished it with 34 seconds left. Granlund had four points, Jackson LaCombe three assists in 30:54.

For Pittsburgh this came a night after Crosby passed Marcel Dionne for sixth on the all-time scoring list, and in a week when Malkin's name is all over the trade-rumor headlines. Malkin had two more assists here. The Penguins will take the process. They won't enjoy the standings.
headline: Gauthier's third hat trick in five games
